clue.text: Month oil spill featured in column

indicators.note: a spill scatters things about, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A month-long oil spill made the news column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Column' looks like a newspaper column; it is a standing stone pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: A monolith is a single great block of stone, often set upright like a pillar or obelisk.

clue.text: Ridicule men of cautious kind, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the following words

blocks.note: the first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at timid, careful men.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock someone is to make fun of them, a straightforward synonym for ridicule as a verb.

clue.text: Scottish man rises, claiming right to be mean

indicators.note: in a down clue, something that rises reads from bottom to top, so backwards
to claim something is to take hold of it, so one piece holds another inside

blocks.note: mon is the Scots form of man
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A Scotsman gets up and asserts his right to be stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' plays on the Scottish stereotype of stinginess, but it is the statistical average.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is the usual or average standard, which is what a mean represents in statistics.

clue.text: Proud peer: Liberal unknown

blocks.note: a lord is a peer of the realm
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
in algebra y is an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A haughty nobleman of the Liberal party nobody has heard of.
explanation.definitionFit: Lordly means arrogant or haughty, behaving with the pride of a nobleman.

clue.text: Course of events affected by increase in marital infidelity

blocks.note: first meaning: the way things are going, an echo of Shakespeare's tide in the affairs of men
second meaning, read literally: a rising wave of extramarital liaisons

explanation.surface: Events take a turn because more spouses are cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from Brutus in Julius Caesar: 'There is a tide in the affairs of men'.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide of affairs is the general drift of circumstances, while read literally a tide of affairs is a surge of adultery.

clue.text: Scanned book about eel fad

indicators.note: about suggests letters moved around, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone skimmed a book about a craze for eels.
explanation.definitionFit: To leaf through a book is to turn its pages quickly, glancing over them, as a quick scan does.

clue.text: One shunning realities, disposed to be the first to arrive

indicators.note: to shun something is to keep away from it, so a letter is left out
disposed here means set out or arranged, so the remaining letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dreamer who avoids reality is the sort to turn up early.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one I from REALITIES to leave REALTIES, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The earliest arrival is whoever gets there before everyone else, so first in time.

clue.text: People toast Rex, who entertains

blocks.note: folk are people
to toast something is to scorch or singe it
R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Guests raise a glass to Rex, their host.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toast' suggests drinking a health; here it means to brown or scorch.
explanation.definitionFit: A folk singer is a performer of traditional songs, someone whose job is to entertain an audience.

clue.text: Disparage people initially getting into fancy code breaking

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the preceding word
fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are worked into a new pattern

blocks.note: to decry is to run down or disparage
the first letter of people
the four letters of into, rearranged

explanation.surface: Mocking those who get into elaborate code-cracking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' looks like a preposition joining the clue; it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Decryption is the act of decoding a cipher, which is exactly what code breaking describes.

clue.text: Shell carried by vehicle to top of hill

blocks.note: a cart is a simple vehicle
a ridge is the crest along the top of a hill

explanation.surface: An artillery shell is hauled up the hill on a truck.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartridge is a casing holding a charge and bullet, which in ammunition is also called a shell.

clue.text: Come in before main tent collapses, causing amusement

indicators.note: a tent that collapses falls into a heap, so its letters end up rearranged

blocks.note: to enter is to come in
these eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting into the big top just as it falls down gives everyone a laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertainment is anything that amuses or diverts an audience, so amusement is a near synonym.

clue.text: Souvenir found in fissure, lichen-covered

indicators.note: found in says the letters are sitting inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the end of fissure and the start of lichen

explanation.surface: An old keepsake turns up in a crack in a rock covered in lichen.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object kept as a reminder of the past, which is what a souvenir is too.

clue.text: Sort of line that's dry and sanguine

blocks.note: a bloodline is a line of descent
being dry means wanting a drink

explanation.surface: A description of some dry and cheerful line of text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sanguine' usually means optimistic; its older sense, from Latin sanguis (blood), is eager for bloodshed.
explanation.definitionFit: In its archaic sense sanguine means bloody or delighting in slaughter, which is what bloodthirsty means.

clue.text: Being against cooking English confit as sweet

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: con as in pros and cons, the case against
E for English plus the six letters of confit, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to making an English confit as a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: Confit is a French dish of meat preserved in fat, an unlikely pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A confection is a sweet treat such as a candy or elaborate dessert.

clue.text: Drama base in holiday spot

blocks.note: a play is a drama
ground as in a base or foundation

explanation.surface: A theatre company has its home at a resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A playground is a place of recreation, and a resort popular with holidaymakers is often called one.

clue.text: Look how self-esteem returns when student's absorbed!

indicators.note: something that returns goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards
to be absorbed is to be taken in, so one letter goes inside

blocks.note: ego is a sense of self-worth
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student's confidence revives once they get immersed in study.
explanation.walkthrough: The student's L-plate is the British sign for a learner driver.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to stare at someone, so it is a particular way to look, usually lecherously.

clue.text: Rotten carcass not untouchable

indicators.note: rotten things break down and fall apart, so the letters are reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A decaying body is something nobody wants to handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not untouchable' looks like a phrase with a double negative; 'not' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sacrosanct is too sacred or important to be interfered with, so it is beyond criticism or change.

clue.text: Test Cockney's hunch about a horse

indicators.note: Cockney speakers famously drop the h at the start of words
about suggests letters moved around, so they are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written before the opening letter goes

explanation.surface: A Londoner checks his gut feeling about a racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney says 'unch for hunch; add that to TEST and rearrange. Cockney is the working-class London accent.
explanation.definitionFit: A chestnut is a horse with a reddish-brown coat, named for the colour.

clue.text: Display support for spring article by Iris

blocks.note: to spring up is to fly or leap
the definite article
flag is a name for the iris plant, as in yellow flag

explanation.surface: Showing backing for a spring piece written by someone called Iris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iris' reads as a woman's name; it is the flower, also called a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly the flag is to show loyalty or promote one's country or cause, so to display support.

clue.text: Some enquired optimistically for an action replay

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used

blocks.note: the end of enquired and the start of optimistically

explanation.surface: A few people hopefully asked to see the incident again.
explanation.definitionFit: A redo is a second go at doing something, so a repeat of an action or replay.

clue.text: Turn new patio into an ideal place

indicators.note: new means made over, so these letters take a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: a U-turn, a turn shaped like the letter
these five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A garden makeover transforms the patio into paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia is Thomas More's imagined perfect society, and now any imagined perfect place.

clue.text: Faith — John Bunyan's hero gets it the first year

indicators.note: the first points to the opening letter of the word after it

blocks.note: Christian is the pilgrim in The Pilgrim's Progress
taken as written
the opening letter of year

explanation.surface: A believer's religion reaches its first anniversary.
explanation.walkthrough: John Bunyan's allegory The Pilgrim's Progress follows Christian's journey to the Celestial City.
explanation.definitionFit: Christianity is a religion, and a faith is a system of religious belief.

clue.text: Sketch of "The Devil's Kitchen"

indicators.note: of here means taken from, so the letters come from within the next words

blocks.note: the end of Devil's and the start of Kitchen

explanation.surface: A drawing of a famous rocky gorge called the Devil's Kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sketch' suggests a drawing; it is a short comic scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a brief comic performance, which is what a sketch is in a revue.

clue.text: Burden that we shall pay for!

blocks.note: first meaning: a responsibility or duty
second meaning, split in two

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words: 'it's on us' means we are paying.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a responsibility or obligation, and read as two words it says the bill falls to us.

clue.text: Bury, turning outsiders away somehow

indicators.note: with the outside letters sent away, only the inner ones remain
somehow says the letters fall into place in some unstated order

blocks.note: the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Burying something, with intruders somehow driven off.
explanation.definitionFit: To inurn is to place ashes in an urn, or more widely to entomb, so to bury.

clue.text: Hide an animal's family

blocks.note: a sheep is an example of an animal
kin are family members

explanation.surface: Concealing a pet's relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb, conceal; it is an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheepskin is the pelt of a sheep, and a hide is the skin of an animal.

clue.text: Untidy criminal in the position of having no cover at all

definitions.text: the position of having no cover at all

indicators.note: criminal means crooked or bent, so the letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A messy crook caught out with no protection at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudity is the state of being naked, wearing no clothes to cover the body.

clue.text: Legendary island where Santa lit fluid

indicators.note: fluid things flow and change shape, so the letters take another form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The mythical isle where Father Christmas set fire to some liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlantis is the island Plato described as sinking beneath the sea, a story taken as myth.
